scientific.integrity: The claim is proved by an explicit complete mode decomposition of the equilateral Kirchhoff star, the published identity B*=-L for Kirchhoff noise, Itô isometry, and elementary harmonic/power-sum asymptotics. The accompanying standard-library replay checks representative subcritical, critical, and supercritical cutoff behavior. The direct 2022 source and the later star/regularity paper were compared at the statement and implication level.
scientific.limitations: The theorem is restricted to an equilateral star, zero potential, unit diffusion, and one unit-variance noisy central Kirchhoff flux. It does not give a universal endpoint law for arbitrary graphs or noise covariances. An equivalent critical coefficient may exist in classical boundary-noise literature under different terminology or normalization.

title: Sharp \(H_{1/4}\) ultraviolet law for central Kirchhoff noise on an equilateral star
